lines.text: In this lesson, you will learn to use event hats (flag, key, click, broadcast) to make programs respond to users, and run several scripts at the same time.
Most apps wait for events — a tap, a key, a message — and then react.
In Scratch, hat blocks start scripts when an event happens.
A sprite can have many scripts.
They run at the same time, like several workers each doing one job.
Broadcast sends a message to every sprite.
Any script with “when I receive” that message starts.
This is how sprites talk to each other.
Web pages do the same thing: button.onclick = startParty.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
